subject: print method for tbl_df displays 100 instead of 10

messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: print method for tbl_df displays 100 instead of 10
parts:
Hi All,

I was surprised to see all 100 observations print from a small tbl_df. When I ran the n up to 1,000 only the first 10 printed as I expected. Bug?

Thanks,
Bob

# For 100 obs, all 100 appear

x <- rnorm(100)
y <- rnorm(100)
df <- data.frame(x, y)
df

tdf <- tbl_df(df)
tdf

# For 1,000, only first 10 appear

x <- rnorm(1000)
y <- rnorm(1000)
df <- data.frame(x, y)
df

tdf <- tbl_df(df)
tdf

messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: Re: print method for tbl_df displays 100 instead of 10
parts: It turns out the cutoff for this behavior is controlled by the option dplyr.print_max, which is set to 100 by default. At 101 observations, the print.tbl_df switches back to displaying only 10. Strange!  Why ever display more than will fit on the screen?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: print method for tbl_df displays 100 instead of 10
parts:
My thought was that if you have a dataset with 11 rows, it's not very
useful to show only the first 10. But I may have extended that
reasoning in an unreasonable way. Maybe dplyr.print_max should be set
to 20 by default? (Unfortunately I don't think there's a standard way
to determine the number of rows available in the console)

Hadley

If you are on OSX or Linux, and isatty(stdout()) is TRUE, then usually
system('tput lines') # or
Sys.getenv("LINES")
is good. If you add API for it on Rstudio, then a lot (most?) of the
users will be covered.
